newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Duma asks government to rethink 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Russia Duma asks government to rethink 1997 budget.

text.p: The Russian State Duma lower house of parliament on Wednesday formally rejected the government's 1997 budget draft at a first reading and asked ministers to rethink it and revise key figures underpinning the plans.
A resolution calling on the government to amend the budget was approved by 262 votes to 83 in the Duma, where communists and their allies are the largest single force.
"Due to the unacceptiblity of the main conceptual ideas of the draft budget...the government of the Russian Federation is asked to change the basic parameters of the budget," the resolution said.
The Duma also agreed to set up a special commission of representatives from the government and from both houses of parliament to reexamine the plans after they are resubmitted.

The Duma first voted on the spending plans on Friday but decided to delay for several days a decision on whether to reject the draft outright or set up a concilliation commission to rework the figures.
The draft envisaged spending of 524.34 trillion roubles, revenues of 433.64 trillion and a deficit of 90.70 trillion, or 3.3 percent of GDP.
